name: Nancowry
catalog_citation: Radhakrishnan, R. 1981. The Nancowry Word: Phonology, Affixal Morphology and Roots of a Nicobarese Language. (Current Inquiry into Language and Linguistics 37.) Edmonton: Linguistic Research Inc. Read via archive.org item micro_IA41153606_0076 (scanned full text).
catalog_quote: 1.2 Placement of stress. The Nancowry words are analyzable into roots and affixes, and the stress occurs always on the root and is not phonetically predictable. Roots are never more than two syllables in length. If the root is disyllabic the stress falls on the second syllable. In this fashion it is seen that, given morphological information, a single rule will place the stress correctly on a form. But, roots may occur with a varying number of intervening affixed syllables. Also, when the vocalic in the stressed syllable is complex (V1V2), only one of the vocalics get stressed, and it could be either V1 or V2. Therefore, the incidence of stress must somehow be marked in the surface representation. However, it could be assigned as shown above by a rule at the underlying level where root identity could be marked.

sources.locator: p. 15 (typological summary), p. 24 (sec. 2 Phonetics/Phonology), p. 25 (sec. 2.3.1), fn. 12-13 (p. 21-22)
sources.note: Only modern (post-1981) description of the language; independent fieldwork confirms stress 'generally fixed on lexical roots' and adds that suffixes are occasionally stressed and that all roots are analysed as monosyllabic -- worth citing as a second source on the record.

sources.quote: fn. 6: 'Stress is perceived, but not found to be phonemic.' p. 106: 'The vowels are found stressed and tensed invariably when they happen to be nucleus of root syllables (compare ... the stressed tensed vowels ... of the respective root syllables ... with the unstressed lax vowels i and e of the respective affixal syllables -si- and -se of the word juɑˑŋsise “progressive”).'
sources.note: Brief phonology preamble states stress is non-phonemic and root syllables are invariably stressed vs lax unstressed affixal syllables; corroborating only.
